cards.title: Introduction to Python Modules
cards.content:
A module is simply a file containing Python code, definitions, and statements. Using modules allows you to logically organize your Python code into separate, manageable files.

You can use any Python source file as a module by executing an import statement in another Python file.

# my_module.py
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

cards.content: To import a specific function called 'sqrt' from the 'math' module, you write: <blank> math import sqrt

cards.title: The Module Search Path
cards.content:
When you import a module, Python searches for it in several locations in a specific order:

  • The directory of the current script
  • The PYTHONPATH (a list of directory names)
  • The standard library directories
  • The site-packages directory of third-party libraries

You can inspect this search path using the sys module:

import sys
print(sys.path)

cards.title: Understanding Python Packages
cards.content:
A package is a way of structuring Python's module namespace by using 'dotted module names'. A directory containing a file named __init__.py is treated as a package by Python.

my_package/
│
├── __init__.py
├── math_operations.py
└── string_operations.py

You can import from a package using dot notation: from my_package import math_operations.
